items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: When I actually played with the Thad Jones and Mel Lewis Band... looking at Snooky Young and Jimmy Nottingham, and Mel Lewis...

ctx.x: But the thing about — I must tell you this. When I actually played with the Thad Jones and Mel Lewis Band, I was so over-awed by the feeling of playing in that band and I couldn’t play for looking at everybody. You know looking at Snooky Young and Jimmy Nottingham, and Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and Jerome Richardson and Joe Farrell and all these people that were in the band. It was just a numbing experience for me. I would like to do it now you know. I would like to really do that again now.
That was quite a roster of — everyone was a soloist.

items.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: found a niche for his distinctive baritone sax in the bands of ... Thad Jones-Mel Lewis

ctx.x: Joe Temperley was born in Cowdenbealth, Scotland in 1929. Jazz became his passion and he took advantage of the playing opportunities available in Scotland and England, including a lengthy stint with the Humphrey-Lyttelton Band. He immigrated to the U.S. in 1965 and found a niche for his distinctive baritone sax in the bands of Woody Herman, Buddy Rich, Thad Jones-Mel Lewis and on numerous recordings. Joe replaced Harry Carney in the Ellington Orchestra and provided a sound that seemed irreplaceable. He currently…
Joe was interviewed at the Jerome Jazz Party in Aspen, Colorado on October 11, 1997, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
